column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
I deeply appreciate how De La Salle continues to honor its Lasallian roots—nurturing faith, compassion, and a sense of service while fostering a strong community. These values are clearly lived and make the College a special place for students to grow holistically.

At the same time, I believe there is an opportunity to further support students in achieving, contributing, and excelling beyond their time at De La Salle. We should continue to encourage and equip them to reach their fullest potential, while also positioning them to gain admission to prestigious post-secondary institutions where they can make an even greater impact in the world. Establishing strong academic foundations and enabling student to get into influential universities serves as a powerful multiplier—amplifying the moral compass and values instilled by De La Salle, and extending that positive influence to the broader community and beyond.  This is a well established formula that has been proven time and time again in politics, in innovation, and how community is shaped.

The post secondary schools we should all strive for:  
Ivy League.
University of Toronto (U of T): engineering, computer science, Rotman Commerce
University of Waterloo – Waterloo, Ontario: computer science, engineering, and co-op
McMaster University – Health Sciences (BHSc)

I did see many student admitted to these in the communications last year.

Tx.

column15: While I commend the school structure course work that help students grow their level of knowledge and inspire students to develop the love of what they are studying, one that really stands out to not achieve anywhere close to that is a Geography assignment to ask students to "dot" the perimeter of countries of the world.  Students face technical difficulties:  one wrong click of a mouse would cause a reset and require to start over.  This causes more than 10 hours to complete the assignment rather than the teacher's claim of a couple of hours. The process made the work like a chore, and upon completion of the assignment when I asked the student what they had learnt, their overall remark was next to nothing.  Instead of work this, it might be worthwhile to talk about why people of different countries have different ways of lives and how they adapt to their local climates.  On the contrary, one assignment within the same subject asking a student to create a town is considered utmost valuable as the student would learn how proper and adequate urban planning drives the economics of a community.  That being said, what that bad assignment did made a significant contributing factor not to pursue further studies in the Geography field, and before the class began it was one of the subjects the student had really looked forward to studying.

column15: I believe academic excellence is starting to wane as compared to the past, with a consistently high teacher turnover rate in the past few years, and many veteran or experienced teachers leaving and being replaced by younger, less experienced and in some instances, less qualified teachers. As well, it appears that many of the younger, less experienced teachers are having a hard time controlling their class (in junior school) and it seems the blame is being placed on students rather than the inability of the teacher to command the respect they deserve, and this becomes apparent when that same cohort does not have any issues with more experienced teachers.

column14: What do you like most about De La Salle College?
column15: We chose this school because of its sense of community rooted in faith and its focus on academic excellence. Although unfortunately based on the turbulence in the last year, there seems to be a rupture in that sense of community,  and academic excellence also seems to be more of an afterthought with a focus placed on hiring teachers who are very much in line with the school’s sense of faith and values, which is absolutely commendable and something to strive for, but worrisome if the teacher proves unqualified - and this has been the case more than once.

column15: Teachers teachers teachers. They are our greatest asset and the ones who will be shaping our students and readying them for future success. Hiring qualified and experienced teachers with a mix of older and younger ones would be ideal. Also, while I am not entirely pleased with the removal of flex mod, I do think that some students in grades 9 and 10 may not be ready to work at such a high level of independence. I am however disappointed to hear that many students in grades 11 and 12 are not satisfied with the new scheduling, as I do think that they should start to learn to schedule their time more independently and it appears that while they have free time, this is quite limited.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15: My son struggled with the reach ahead math curriculum since he started in grade 6. By grade 8, this curriculum, which was grade 9 "with a sprinkle of grade 10 math" was extremely challenging for him. He worked hours every night on homework, attend regular tutorials and still just passed. I was aware of  quite a few students from this grade that struggled like him if not worse, regularly getting below 50% on tests and quizzes. By the last term of the year, he was demoralized by putting in so much effort and not seeing his grades or learning improve. Although he did well in all his other subjects, there was so much intense focus on math for him that he became extremely stressed about it. I was concerned that he would not pass the course in that he could barely keep up 50's in the class by that time of year. The teacher explained that students are not held back and that his grades didn't matter, it was the experience and exposure to the curriculum which he would redo in grade 9 anyway. The rationale for this is to the detriment of these young people who are not developmentally ready for the gr. 9 math curriculum. He and other classmates who struggled saw themselves as not smart, not as capable as those who "got it". I'm not sure why any grade 10 math should have even been explored by the time most were drowning in that class. This course affected my son's self-esteem and self-worth in such a negative way it was hard for him to see his successes in other subjects. This impression has carried with him into this school year. I hope, in due time, he will be able to put the experience behind him and see himself in a different light. Review of the gr. 8 math curriculum would be wise.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
First of all, I think the school is doing an amazing job and there are always areas to improve.
For faith, I think the school does a wonderful job at teaching the fundamentals but needs more work on making faith more attractive to the students.  Faith is "catchy" as Brother Peter once said, so perhaps more zeal is need to inspire students to live faith out in their daily lives.  I don't know the answer to this one!

Parent teacher interview process.  Can we get this online?

Teaching continuously comes back as an issue depending on the stream.  Science being an issue and more recently have heard of University students in first year Chemistry who are struggling as they did not have sufficient background.  French has also been identified as an issue in the senior grades.  Music program is right on the level and I think the school could do better.
I know teacher retention across the board is difficult but given we are demanding high academic standards from our students, I think it is only fundamental that we would have the same standards for the teachers.

column14: What do you like most about De La Salle College?
column15: With one student who has graduated and two in high school, I really like how each child has been able to shape a high school experience that is unique to their interests and abilities. They have all formed meaningful friendships with their classmates and connections with many of their teachers. In general, the teachers are excellent and available outside of classroom hours for academic support. They have been well-supported by their guidance counsellors. The academic rigour has prepared them/is preparing them for university.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
In no particular order:
- The Schoology/Powerschool/Del email is a lot for students to manage. A simpler way of communicating, where it all happens on one platform, would help. 
- It would be great to take advantage of the house system, eg group some orientation events for new students by house, maybe have inter-house sports teams, both to build community and create team sport opportunities for kids who can't commit to varsity teams because of other activities, or aren't yet at the varsity level
- The parent class representative model might benefit from some changes. It seems that parent reps are chosen in Grade 5 and in general remain the class reps till Grade 12. This can limit the involvement of new parents at every stage, creates a huge amount of work for those who are reps for repeated years, and also limits fresh perspectives. Having staggered two year terms for parent reps would allow continuity and bring in new people each year.
- When our first Del student started, we asked many people questions about the school's governance model and its Board of Directors, etc and were surprised that no one seemed to have this information. Recently it has been shared quite extensively with the community. It does not seem to be best governance practice to have unlimited terms for Board members - if I am right several have been in their roles for 20+ years. A refresh of this system seems necessary
- We were disappointed that several times, history classes were cancelled for lack of interest. The school has an excellent focus on sciences and math. It could work on supporting the arts courses as well, English, history, languages etc. It is great to see that the school is supporting the music and band program - for a period, it felt like it was relegated to a less important role.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Over the past few years, we have observed a concerning decline in teacher quality, competence, and retention. While it may be admirable to give unqualified or inexperienced teachers an opportunity — and as a Catholic school we are called to act with charity — this cannot come at the expense of our children’s education, well-being, and future.

Our students deserve teachers who are not only caring, but also well-trained, confident, and capable of meeting diverse learning and emotional needs. When new or inexperienced teachers are hired, or when concerns are raised by parents, the school has a responsibility to provide additional support — for both the teacher and the students.

There must be a clear onboarding and mentorship program that actively monitors, evaluates, and supports teachers as they grow into their roles. Leaving teachers to struggle without proper guidance harms everyone — students lose valuable learning opportunities, and teachers become discouraged and are more likely to leave.

If we truly value education, we must value our educators. That means prioritizing the hiring of qualified, experienced teachers, and creating a culture where all staff are supported to succeed.

In addition, the new schedule does not work — particularly for the junior school. It is confusing, difficult to follow, and fails to provide adequate time for all subjects. Key academic areas should not be taught only once every five days. This structure undermines consistent learning and makes it harder for both students and teachers to maintain focus, continuity, and progress.

column15:
1) hold retreats/seminars regarding pragmatic examples of implementing God's way during teenage life - e.g. how to respond to exposures to alcohol, drugs, sex including oral sex, exclusive cliques, bullying, online content; discuss safer sex during sex education including but not exclusive to Catholic teachings regarding sex
2) be aware and on the lookout for bullying with zero tolerance for bullying at school, with suspensions and expulsions given accordingly
3) improve cafeteria options to be more nutritious; consider standard cafeteria meals as part of tuition for all to enjoy (e.g. I've heard amazing reviews about food services at UCC)

It would be good to address these behaviours directly with the student body to give them guidance of how to respond when exposed to situations like this and how to act in ways that are kind and not hurtful or harmful to themselves or others and that are consistent with the values of Christ.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15: Workload can be demanding at times. More focus on mental/health and well-being would be helpful. New schedule is hard for the children to establish consistency / routines as they have different classes each week. Additionally, in grade 8, we’re finding it does not provide sufficient class time for important subjects like science and over-emphasizes some art subjects. As a result, the science teacher is often behind on the curriculum and moving assessment dates. Grade 11 is noting there is a lot less time to complete work at school and few breaks. Additionally, this year we have noted some issues with a few new teachers who do not have experience teaching (grade 8 science and grade 11 computers). The children are not learning in class, self-teaching and growing frustrated and while issues have been raised with administration by many parents, it doesn’t seem like there are improvements.

column15:
Academic Focus and Teaching Quality:
One of the main reasons we chose Del was its emphasis on core learning—math, the sciences, and the arts. I believe deeply in equipping children with a solid mastery of the fundamentals so they can build confidently from there. However, somewhere along the way, it feels like the joy of learning has been lost. Curiosity, creativity, and genuine intellectual engagement should be nurtured, not stifled.

It may be time to introduce teacher reviews or feedback mechanisms that assess not just performance, but inspiration—who sparks curiosity and confidence in students, and who simply goes through the motions or discourages them.

Academic Support:
We were assured that if our child ever struggled, there would be support—that teachers would step in, provide extra help, and, if needed, require attendance at tutorials or office hours. I was even advised not to hire an outside tutor, as the school would handle it.

That hasn’t been our experience. While my child thrives in some subjects and has even been offered AP opportunities, they continue to struggle in others—and the promised academic support simply hasn’t materialized.

Athletics and the Whole-Child Philosophy:
When we joined Del, we were drawn to the promise of developing the whole child—with athletics positioned as a key part of that commitment. Unfortunately, the current approach to sports feels inconsistent and half-hearted.

Watching your child head into a game saying, “We’re going to get killed,” over and over isn’t just disheartening—it chips away at their confidence and sense of team spirit. Athletics should be an opportunity to build resilience, pride, and belonging, not a reminder of uneven investment or lack of preparation.

column15:
Communication:
Communication from the school to parents is inconsistent and often unclear. Updates frequently lack focus, detail, and timeliness, leaving families unsure of key information or next steps.

Culture and Attitude:
There is a noticeable sense of "haughty" within administration and some faculty—an attitude that feels at odds with the school’s stated values. A former parent I spoke with, whose children have since graduated, described their experience as “torture”—despite their kids now thriving at university. We both remarked that the prevailing tone from the school often feels like, “You’re lucky to be here, so don’t complain.” Unfortunately, that resonates with my own experience.

Website and Parent Portal:
The website and parent portal are outdated, confusing, and rarely accurate. Incorrect schedules and year calendars remain posted for months, making it difficult to rely on the information provided. In this day and age, it wouldn’t take much—perhaps hiring a student, alum, or professional—to make these resources functional and user-friendly.

Student Support Services:
Having toured several other schools before choosing Del, I can say with confidence that the level of student support offered here falls short by comparison. Other schools provide far more depth and individualized attention. As our child begins to think about university, this gap in support is increasingly concerning. The recent grade 11 evening sponsored by them was below a standard I would have expected for a school of Del's standard.

column15:
The Admissions office could benefit from a significant refresh. It’s difficult to tell whether the lack of transparency is intentional or simply the result of poor process design—but either way, it leaves a negative impression. There’s a noticeable tone of haughtiness that feels inconsistent with the school’s faith-based values. Pride in the school is understandable, but an attitude of “you should feel lucky to be here” is not the right message for a community built on humility and belonging.

When my other child went through the admissions process, it left them feeling discouraged in a way none of the other schools did—which should never be the outcome of a faith-centered environment.

Finally:

I don’t like that my tone feels negative—because this feedback comes from a place of genuine care and hope for improvement. But after years of raising these concerns, with little visible progress, it’s hard not to feel discouraged.

Many parents share similar frustrations, though most discuss them quietly, wary of speaking up. There’s a real fear—especially among newer families—that voicing concerns will make no difference, or worse, reflect poorly on their children. That dynamic alone should be cause for reflection.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15: Communication from the school is relatively disorganized and, in many cases, does not provide parents with sufficient advance notice of upcoming events.  Particularly for parents of new students who are not familiar with the school and its traditions, official communications should be more timely and a little more comprehensive (with sufficient background information and explanation).  Consideration should be given to running a "B" team for extra-curricular sports teams in order to provide students who may not be top-level athletics with an opportunity to participate.  Also, very early morning practices school be avoided.  High school students need sufficient sleep for their health and well-being and it's simply not possible for them to get enough sleep with hours of homework and then a morning practice at 7am.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15: The jump to Del in grade 9 has been a big one for our child. It would be amazing if Student Services could provide weekly touch bases for new students (compulsory) that supported with executive planning/organizing, and to encourage participation in extracurriculars, liase with teachers, etc. Just for the first few months as students find their footing. Our child is so focused on keeping on top of his course work that he may be missing out on some of the bigger picture skills and opportunities at Del, and I think having a regular touchpoint and building a rapport with a student advisor (or perhaps even an older student as a designated mentor) would be a great way for him to develop organizational skills and confidence / motivation to connect more with what the school offers. With only 4 years of high school, I think this would accelerate new students' orientation and settling in so they can maximize their time at Del.

column15: There seems to be very little communicated about the extracurriculars at the school. Propose a "fair" of sorts where the various clubs, extracurriculars, etc. set up so new students can learn about them. And also would love it if new students to the school were more actively "recruited". The extracurriculars are so important, expecially for new students looking to make friends, and considering the daily schedule with ALTs vs. ILTs in grade 9 limits socializing during the school day. Would even propose that extracurriculars be mandatory at the school.  Also, intramural sports would be great, for students who aren't candidates for the Del sports teams yet still want to participate in an activity. And the opportunity for students to propose clubs would be great as well!

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
There needs to be stronger communication and a shared understanding of the bigger vision across the school, rather than an overemphasis on rigid rules or minor disciplinary issues, like detentions for shoes. Small measures only work when they are connected to a clear, overarching purpose. This vision should guide every aspect of the school experience, ensuring that policies, teaching, and expectations are aligned and meaningful.

Investing in more qualified teachers and cohesive planning across grade levels is essential to achieve this. Teaching should be informed by how boys and girls learn differently, with strategies that reflect these differences rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach. Reducing power imbalances between teachers and students will create a more respectful and supportive learning environment.

Ultimately, the focus should be on cultivating academic excellence and personal growth, rather than enforcing rigid rules. When the school’s vision is consistently applied and connected across all areas, students benefit from both a structured and inspiring environment where learning and development are prioritized.

column15:
Vision

Create a cohesive, inspiring learning environment where the school’s vision connects across all policies, teaching practices, and student experiences. Focus on academic excellence, personal growth, and meaningful engagement rather than rigid rules or minor disciplinary measures.


1. Clear, Shared Vision

Goal: Ensure all staff, students, and parents understand and engage with the school’s overarching vision.
Strategies:

* Communicate a clear vision statement at the start of the year.
* Hold quarterly staff meetings and student assemblies to review vision alignment.
* Include vision reminders in newsletters and school communications.

2. Focused, Purposeful Discipline

Goal:Shift from minor, rigid rule enforcement to discipline that supports learning and growth.
Strategies:
Review and revise disciplinary policies to remove non-academic punishments.
Introduce restorative practices and provide teacher training in supportive discipline.

3. Teacher Quality & Cohesive Planning
Goal: Improve teaching effectiveness and cross-grade alignment.
Strategies: Hire OCT Teachers. or specialists that have taught 

* Provide ongoing professional development and mentorship programs.
* Implement structured planning sessions across grade levels.
* Regularly review curriculum alignment between grades.

4. Gender-Sensitive Learning Approaches

Goal:Address different learning styles of boys and girls.
Strategies:

* Conduct teacher training on gender-based learning differences.
* Introduce differentiated instruction in classrooms.
* Monitor student engagement and adjust teaching strategies accordingly.

5. Reduce Teacher-Student Power Imbalances

Goal:Foster respectful, collaborative classroom environments.
Strategies:

* Establish student advisory councils and feedback sessions.
* Encourage collaborative classroom decision-making.
* Provide equity-focused teacher training.

6. Academic Focus and Excellence

Goal: Prioritize meaningful learning and measurable academic progress.
Strategies: Lead By example not top down 

* Set clear learning goals for each grade and track progress.
* Align classroom activities with skill-building rather than rule enforcement.
* Celebrate academic achievements and improvements school-wide.

These minor policies only have real impact when they connect to a bigger mission that everyone understands. A unified vision should shape every part of school life—policies, teaching, and expectations—so they all work toward something meaningful.  

Building this kind of alignment also depends on hiring strong, well-trained educators and creating consistent planning across grade levels. Teaching should reflect an understanding of how boys and girls may learn differently, rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all method. Reducing the hierarchy between teachers and students can also help foster an environment of mutual respect and genuine support.  

Ultimately, the goal should be to nurture both academic achievement and personal development—not to enforce rigidity for its own sake. When a school’s guiding vision is woven into everything it does, students thrive within an atmosphere that’s both structured and inspiring, where learning and growth naturally go hand in hand.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
- more time for students to get between classes
- some ILT time would be good
- opportunities to participate in sports teams appear to be very limited and restricted to students who are already involved in the sport outside of school; some sporting activities would provide an opportunity for students to get to know each other 
- some evenings, my daughter has homework from all of her classes or multiple tests the next day. With an after school club, this means that she is up very late doing homework. Sleep is important for students in high school. Some coordination between teachers would be good (I'm not against homework and students learning time management - this is important - but sleep is also important). Once a week late start might be good.
- for students starting in grade 9, additional support for some subjects would be welcome (as the Del students have been working ahead, my daughter is behind in some subjects like math and has found it difficult to get support even when attending tutorials).

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
-I think there should be a way to have a common calendar so that too many assessments don't fall on the same day for the students.
-Better communication is needed as sometimes decisions are made by people who aren't as well versed in the subject I teach and make decisions that have great impact.
-Late starts for staff would be helpful on days when we have 2 back to back P/T interview evenings or Open House as it is very difficult for our wellbeing to be at the school for long hours and to have to teach the next day.
-P/T interviews process at this school is difficult - a discussion about its structure with the staff would be appreciated to look at other options.

column14: Any additional comments about your experience or the College?
column15:
-Acknowledgement/appreciation of staff service would be encouraging. For instance, on the last day of the previous year, I was speaking to a colleague who had just completed 25 years of teaching at Del but the year ended without celebrating that (at least not to my knowledge) which was very sad to see.
-I write this lovingly but being seen/appreciated is something that I think Del can do better; I don't think the multiple changes and challenges and their impacts, that happened over the last few years is recognized. Every year has looked so drastically different which inevitably leaves a toll, but some of us stayed loyal and stuck through it.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
- If a student doesn't make a sports team, there should be some way that student can be part of a program that helps them improve in that sport. At the moment, if the student does not make the team, then they're not able to practice that sport for the remainder of the season. Maybe a B-team?

Appropriate "crime" vs "punishment" - We've seen that detentions are assigned for what we deem to be minimal offences, and especially for new students, who are still adjusting, a reminder of the rules might benefit the students more than just handing out detentions for forgetting a book in a locker for example.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
As a female teacher working at this school, it feels very unrealistic to see myself staying here long-term. For example, parent–teacher interviews run until 9 p.m., and most staff do not live close to the school due to the high cost of living in the area. This means many evenings are spent commuting and committing additional time to the school instead of being with our families.
If the expectation is to attract and retain authentic Catholic teachers who value family life, it is concerning that the current structure does not support that same value for staff. Teachers are carrying numerous additional responsibilities, and the volume of extracurricular commitments is overwhelming. I truly want to spend time with students outside of class, but the travel, preparation, and number of evenings required make it unsustainable.
At this school, there is effectively no work–life balance. This is a major reason why teacher turnover is so high—it is simply not realistic to maintain this workload long-term.
I believe the school would benefit from additional administrative roles specifically designed to support teachers, or from hiring more outside coaches and staff to reduce our load. Another possible solution is providing rental spaces or accommodations for staff who live far away, which would greatly ease the burden of long commutes combined with late evenings.
These changes would help create a healthier, more sustainable environment for teachers and ultimately benefit the entire school community.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
New teachers / new staff - In my view, all teachers teaching children should be qualified teachers (OCT); it's concerning when they are not (although I do understand that some subjects like accounting, etc might not be OCT). I believe any new teachers/ staff need a buddy/ mentor; they need to be supervised and mentored to make sure that they are effectively communicating with the children (Grade 7 science teacher is an issue; it's what keeps me worrying and up at night)

Grade 7 science teacher - there is a lot of confusion in Grade 7 science about what the deadlines are and this is a pattern - not a one off; also the science class in Grade 7 is very noisy and it is difficult for the children to concentrate b/c of the noise and talking; the Grade 7 science teacher is not a Ontario College of Teachers Graduate - this is concerning given the importance of science and the problems just described. Concerned that the grade 7 students will have gaps in their science learning and also seems the expectation is for the students to teach themselves (they are too young for this type of learning; it should not be university learning). Finally, it is my impression that this teacher is throwing around detentions, warnings, etc as a way to get control of the class. However, these same children who get the detentions/ warnings are not having problems in the other classes with the other teachers. I do not like "threats" to get control of the class; my preference would be that the teacher is engaging and has the respect of the students to create a safe/ happy / positive learning environment where the children are inspired. 

Science at del - understand that science at del might not prepare students for university; this is concerning and needs attention at the school; please can you add focus to this area when planning for next year to make sure that the reputation of the school is upheld? Very concerned with what I have heard about high school chemistry and Grade 7 science this year is a huge issue. 

New high school schedule - the new high school schedule seems to have impacted the junior school schedule - we understood that the junior school schedule would not be impacted, but it was since certain subjects do not happen as often now; also the 8 day schedule is tricky for junior school students (a 5 day schedule would be better); can you revert the junior school schedule to the PY model since it was not broken? 

Grade 7 homework board - teachers are not consistently using the homework board (some are, some aren't); please can all the teachers use the homework board so that the students copy down their homework, deadlines, and upcoming tests/ quizzes? 

Uniform - would be nice if the students could wear a golf shirt in the summer months (maybe on specific days of the week)

Teacher job postings - I heard that no teacher job openings were posted at the end of last school year (for the 25/ 26 school year); posting jobs ensures fairness, transparency, and also a competitive environment to ensure that the best teachers are attracted to del (a fantastic school); if jobs aren't posted, the top candidates (in science for example) won't be attracted to apply at del; I recommend teacher openings are posted going forward

column15:
-  Science department / grade 7 science teacher - currently the science department has a poor reputation among the parents; del needs the reputation that the science department is top notch (del has a great academic / university readiness reputation, but needs to improve in the area of science)
- Music department - it is a huge loss that Ms. Di Nardo left the school; a head of music who is inspiring and musically motivating needs to be recruited
- DECA club - the students in this club need "crash course" days in their assigned subject day so that they are better prepared (esp for the students in grade 9 and 10 who haven't taken business courses yet)? This club is an amazing opportunity for the students, but having them go to the competition day better prepared would go a long way
- cafeteria food (high quality, tasty food that varies by days of the week is needed); also the hours of the cafeteria need to be slightly extended so that the students can get a snack after school and also before school (esp if students get to school early)
- school schedule - the junior school schedule should be restored to what it was; the high school schedule should be looked at also b/c some of the classes are too long
- Teacher openings - these positions should be posted publicly to attract the best teacher candidates to the position to uphold the academic reputation of the college (to have the best teachers!).
- Grade book - would be nice if the grade book was open 1x a month to keep track of students' progress

If the students had difficulty understanding their projects in class, they found it hard to do their homework at home. Please make an efficient environment, for example, set up a meeting between the teacher and the students instead of asking parents' opinions about the teacher. I have a son who is a quiet boy and not very confident in talking in public. I hope the teacher can find the opportunity to make him feel comfortable talking in class or at school.

Have a half-day trip to the beautiful church or the historical neighbourhood in the city. Walking and chatting are good experiences for any grade's teachers and students.

column14: What do you like most about De La Salle College?
column15: High standards that are expected for the students. Strong lines of communication between school and families. Faith dimension, upholding Christian values in spite of social challenges that are sometimes contrary to our values. Balance between learning with and through technology and paper and pencil tasks and learning. Tight knit community where everyone knows one another - it feels like home away from home for the students. Various clubs that make students feel included - no matter what their areas of may be - they will find a club that suits their interests. And finally, the potential that is seen in every student, and the support that is given to them as they prepare to leave the schools. The teachers and staff are very special people.

column14: Any additional comments about your experience or the College?
column15: We have been blessed to call Del home since 2019, and are sad that this is our final year at the college. While no school or institution is perfect, we are fortunate to have had our children experience a De La Salle education - it has been formative and transformational. We appreciate the staff and their tireless work - especially Brother, Mr. Lundy, Ms. Carreco and Mr. Stratton. The tenured teachers like Mr. Sourial, Mr. Pupo and Mr. Schaeffer have raised the bar for education and challenged our children in ways that have opened their eyes to the realities of hard work and merit. We pray that the college may continue to do this for generations of students after ours.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
- proper library that promotes student reading, research and has individual and group quiet spaces to study
-a policy on AI and Tech Education (not EdTech) and supporting. curriculum
-a weekly schedule that is analagous to the university schedule and their extra-curricular activities.  university courses are offered for example MWF or TTH or once a week for three hours.  Between holidays and special school days the schedules constantly change.  Having to keep up with those changes and how they impact extra-curriculars and jobs does not mimic real life situations at university or the work environment which tend to be weekly. 
-i would advocate for a unified highschool lunch that allowed for house intra-murals duringg some lunches and clubs at other lunch times.
-advocate for more experiential learning in field trips and guest speakers
-monthly awards for students per grade/class highlighting the virtues
-curriculum across the disciplines that teaches students more about digital citizenship, mindful media use, dignity of the person
-choose ways to gather parents that promotes the mission of the school. Instead of socials at pubs why not grade mass with the parents and students. it is a better way to meet your child's peers and their parents. Father/daughter dance and Mother/Son mass and luncheon
-choose ways to celebrate academic achievement that inspires other students to work harder and to celebrate their peers.  Awards should be presented at school during the day.  Is the award for the parent or to highlight the student in their community of learning.
-a proper and traditional way to celebrate advent - a live nativity scene and a market place that doesn't sell much is very commercial.  Most of the other private schools have a proper advent carols and reflections/lessons that are mainstays of the school's traditions.  They cultivate a sense of pride in the school culture and alumni often look to these moments to also participate and support the school.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
We are committed to our children’s education and deeply value the school community. In that spirit, I would like to share a few concerns and corresponding suggestions that I hope will be considered.

1. School Health, Educational Quality, and Rebuilding Trust
While transparency has improved this year, we still feel concerned about the school’s overall health — particularly academic consistency, staff stability, and school culture. These areas have created uncertainty and a loss of trust among families, including ours. A strong academic environment and stable culture are what drew our family to De La Salle in the first place.
To help strengthen confidence in the school, I suggest:
• Communicate more transparently about priorities and changes,
• Provide meaningful opportunities for parent feedback (thank you for this survey), and
• Strengthen alignment between leadership, teachers, and families through regular updates.

2. High Staff Turnover
Teacher turnover has been quite high in recent years, and continuity is essential for strong learning outcomes and a positive school culture. I encourage the school to:
•	Review the causes of staff attrition and address them proactively,
•	Ensure compensation and professional development opportunities are competitive to attract teachers that have appropriate qualifications and experience,
•	Implement a more robust mentorship/shadowing program to support new teachers, and 
•	Implement a more effective teacher retention program.

3. Communication Regarding Academic Progress
Communication about student progress can sometimes feel limited. More regular, proactive updates would allow parents to support learning at home in a timely manner, prevent small concerns from becoming larger issues, and reinforce shared accountability between students, families, and educators.  While student independence is important, parents are ultimately responsible for supporting their child’s academic development and should have clearer, more consistent access to this information. Please consider making grades and/or teacher feedback available to parents on PowerSchool throughout the year and encourage teachers to provide more frequent updates via phone/email to all students, including students doing well over 80%.

4. Parent–Teacher Interview Format
Five minutes per interview is insufficient to have meaningful discussion about student progress. Extending the allotted time or offering alternative formats would greatly improve the quality of communication.

5. Interview Booking System
Coordinating interviews across multiple teachers and siblings is challenging under the current system. An online scheduling platform would allow parents to book times efficiently and ensure meetings work for both families and teachers.

6. Communication Regarding Sports and Clubs
It would be very helpful for families to receive clear and consistent communication about sports and clubs, including tryout dates, practice schedules, game/meet times, and any schedule changes. Email updates would allow parents to better plan pickups and drop-offs. While some coaches already provide this information, the approach is inconsistent. Schoology calendar lists some activities, but the calendar is not customized to reflect the specific clubs or teams a student is registered for, limiting its usefulness.

7. Improvements to the Parent Portal
The Parent Portal could be strengthened to better support communication between parents and the school. Currently, it is difficult to locate essential information such as teacher and staff contact details (emails), sports and club information, and tutorial schedules. Improving the structure and accessibility of this platform would provide parents with a more reliable and centralized source of information.

8. Cafeteria Food Quality
There has been an ongoing concern regarding the quality of cafeteria meals. Consider implementing periodic quality inspection of the food and/or consider changing the vendor.

column14: What do you like most about De La Salle College?
column15: We love the high level of academic excellence, we note the teachers who care very much for their students, who are available for help when needed, above all, the core mission of teaching the Christian values and virtues, and helping students to be servant-leaders during and after their time at the school. We love the aspect of prayer, school masses, class masses, Eucharistic Adoration, all of these things that provide grounding and centeredness for the spiritual life of the school. When we out God first, we remember our mission, and everything that we do has that greater purpose, outside of ourselves, and we see Jesus in our neighbour, our efforts, our volunteer work, our drive to be doctors, lawyers, police men and women etc, they take on greater purpose because we see how we can contribute to the overall success of society, and to preserving and upholding the human dignity of each person created in God's image and likeness, through our actions and the lives we choose to live.

column15: Please encourage and foster a spirit of openness to youth knowing about, being introduced to, and exploring the different kinds of vocations, single, married and especially religious life and the priesthood. It's important to introduce, obviously not to push, but a gentle introduction goes a long way to perhaps lighting that spark down the road. For the next President, please consider a candidate who is a Brother, or who works know the Lasallian mission by heart, selfless in action and mission, having the students as the main motivation for their work at the school, and of course, God as the core and centre of the life and work. Throughout their long history, the Brothers have given their life to the students and the school,  and wouldn't it be wonderful to see the Brothers working at the school, being an example and role models to the students of the very core of the Lasallian mission: forming leaders and Saints, and preparing them not only for academic, the workforce and their communities, but also preparing their souls for Heaven.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
I think the school could benefit from a more balanced approach to discipline. Havin a Discipline Director and a Vice Principal focused on discipline feels a bit excessive, and it can make the environment feel stricter than it needs to be. A friendlier, more supportive tone would go a long way.
I also feel that some members of the leadership team (namely, Rouselle) could be more approachable. There are times when they come across as distant or as if they are above the students and the parent, which makes it hard for people to feel comfortable asking for help or having an honest conversation. A warmer, more down-to-earth presence from leadership would really help students feel supported and heard.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
The school really needs to focus on hiring a principal who is approachable, engaged, and present in the community. Someone like Mr. Lundy made a huge difference because families felt comfortable and heard. I worry that hiring Mr. Rouselle will take the school back to the Voustinos days (which were AWFUL for the students, when there was no real open-door policy and leadership felt distant. Both of these supposed "leaders" are pompous. Bring in someone like Stratton, who is young and approachable. Remember that an open door policy is best, especially with all the pressure in and outside school that students are facing.  
 It is time to rethink Prize Night. It tends to highlight the same small group every year, and it would be nice to see a more inclusive way of recognizing a wider range of students.

The board is another area that needs attention. It has been the same people for far too long (generally speaking no-one sits on a board for more than 5 years, and there are clear conflicts of interest, for instance students being expected to raise funds for a charity connected to a board member (Denise). That does not feel right. Some fresh voices and new leadership would be a healthy change.

Overall, it is 2025. The school needs to move away from some of the outdated attitudes that still linger and start embracing change in a meaningful way.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15: Much can be said, but I will focus on two things: administration concerns and classroom priority.  Regarding the administration, it seems clear to many of us that there is a breakdown of communication between the various levels and roles in the administration.  Each is individually someone who loves the school, but they are simply too compartmentalized and do not talk to one another.  There is a clear problem at the leadership level regarding accountability.  Event planning requires all the stakeholders to be at the table having an open dialogue about best practices and animating the events.  Planning seems to be adhoc and improvised.  Last minute scheduling changes and unspecific instructions create gaps and open things up to frustration for the staff trying to do their jobs.  The second concern is with classroom priority.  There are simply too many interruptions and cocurricular demands on students that severely impact the building of any sort of momentum or routine.  Morning assembly routinely goes long stealing time from period 1.  AP exams essentially eliminate many students from senior classes throughout the months of April and May, and the cocurricular schedule is simply too much, especially in the winter for skiing and swimming, and the spring.  There are also too many clubs running that are competing with the same students.  While I appreciate that we are trying to get students involved in cocurricular activities, the consequences are really impacting the classroom experience for both students and staff.  One of the motivating factors about a return to a more consistent block schedule was that kids were not experiencing a more routine day, being in class regularly.  I can tell you that my experience is that, especially in these weeks since Easter, there has been no routine and there has been little to no momentum building towards exams.  At a time when we need more calm, we are experiencing the opposite.

column15: The Catholic Faith community.  The fact that we offer mass almost daily and that faith is not just ornamental here.  This needs to continue to be front and center of what we do here.  Families need to understand that this is a Catholic school and we are unashamed of that.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15: Less non-classroom related activities.  Yes, we ought to have sports and clubs and school-wide community events - but these should not impact the daily classroom routine.  Breaks is the rigor of the classroom are good, but they should occur regularly and strategically.  We are constantly making exceptions (exceptions to morning assembly, exceptions to missed classes, exceptions to accommodate missed classes).  Guess what, constant exceptions are no longer exceptions - it is now the norm.  And our new normal is, simply put: constant changes, interruptions, missed classes, and extended assemblies.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Some teachers at the school are not effective at communicating material or maintaining a positive classroom environment. Ms. Scavone, despite being a supply teacher, has reportedly been removed from teaching Grade 7 science multiple times, which raises concerns about teaching quality and consistency. Many students feel that her classes do not contribute positively to their learning experience.

Ms. Meli’s teaching style has also discouraged students from pursuing or participating in art classes. Instead of inspiring creativity and interest in the subject, many students leave feeling unmotivated and disengaged. Teachers should encourage students and help them grow confidence in their abilities, not make them lose interest in subjects they once enjoyed.

De La Salle College should focus its resources on teachers who create supportive, effective, and engaging learning environments. Improving accountability and listening more closely to student feedback would help improve the overall school atmosphere and educational experience.

column15: It is some simple things - a lot of complaints about bathrooms being dirty and unusable.  Water fountains dispensing warm and cloudy water - food in the cafeteria being extremely expensive - bordering on prices seen at sporting events and venues.  As well,  the cancelling of extra curricular programs because of low attendance is disappointing - perhaps children can be allowed to play up to next level. think raising tuition by $1,000–$1,500 per child could significantly help enhance the overall experience for students. Another concern we sometimes hear from our children is that certain teachers repeatedly yell at students and use threatening language. We do not feel this fosters a positive, inclusive, or supportive learning environment. We fully understand that when students behave inappropriately there should be consequences, such as detentions or other appropriate disciplinary measures, but yelling and comments such as “I’m going to make you run until you guys throw up” seem excessive and somewhat archaic to us. column15: One of the reasons we chose DEL  apart from academics, faith and community was because of the no phone, no screen policy. but this seems to have changed and I noticed that while I was volunteering at school many, many were playing vido games on tablets, Ipads and phones in lunch room. I would prefer a complete ban on screens. I raised this in the meeting in early March with the other parents  and we all unanimously agreed. I know that my son spends a lot of time on his computer at school and much of it is on a game. If you had a blanket rule, no screens it would remove policing and people would be more engaged. There is also no reason while at school to be on a screen, Notes and lessons are posted. engagement would be better. These are more addictive than crack cocaine.

To help the college improve on bridging the home to school connection, a more timely response by teachers and staff to emails and inquiries would be greatly appreciated. column15: What De La Salle College school should improve most is its disciplinary approach. The fact that students can get a one hour detention, without notifying a parent or guarding, which requires them to sit and stare at a wall after school is highly punitive. After only 2 minor infractions; such as being a couple of minutes late to a class or a uniform infraction; a detention for a one hour duration is not fair, unjust, and undeserved. If the well-being of children and a nurturing environment is what matter to De La Salle college, a reflection and change to discipline is warranted.

After school clubs could also include languages: French, Italian, Latin etc. for children to practice their language skills. Also, using more opportunities to include meaningful opportunities for students to engage in languages could be explored. Such as : cinema francophone or Carnaval de Quebec.  The gr 5 French materials did not provide any speaking or reading opportunities in French as outlined in the Ontario Curriculum.  This is disappointing  as we are a bilingual country. Even the representative that visited from the DEL from France noted that the students and teacher do not speak a word of French in class when he observed the class- specifically the gr.5 class. He spoke with my child after class and asked if it was common for the teacher to teach French speaking English.  My child replied yes, the teacher instructional language is always in English. This is not how someone learns a language. 


For the junior grades, gr. 5 and 6, provide the boys the opportunity to wear shorts as part of the uniform for September/October and May/June. The boys overheat easily in the warmer months as they still play hard at recess.  This would be in the style of British/European private school uniforms.

column15:
While I do believe my children will be very well prepared for university academically, I do have concerns about how exceptionally demanding the grading environment can be. Admission averages for many university programs are now extremely competitive, and at times it can feel almost impossible for students to achieve the grades required for the programs they aspire to pursue, despite working incredibly hard. Striking a balance between academic rigor and ensuring students remain competitive in university admissions is something the school should continue to reflect on.

 The school could also do a better job of recognizing a broader range of students. Too often, the same students are repeatedly highlighted and celebrated, while many others who contribute meaningfully both inside and outside of the school community go unnoticed. Expanding recognition to include different types of achievement, leadership, involvement, character, and personal growth would help create a more inclusive and encouraging school culture. 

 Both the Parent Association and the school tend to repeat many of the same events and initiatives year after year. Bringing in new ideas, refreshing traditions, and creating more opportunities tailored to older students and families would help keep the community engaged and allow the school to continue evolving in a positive way.

#1 The friendships my children have developed during their time at the school have been incredibly meaningful and lasting.
#2 Many of the younger teachers, particularly in math and science, have brought a more student-centered and supportive approach to teaching. The strongest teachers are the ones who genuinely care about their students, are approachable, responsive, and have strong teaching experience and subject knowledge.
#3 The departure of Mr. Voutsinos, and soon Brother Domenic, represents an important opportunity for the school to continue moving away from a more rigid and outdated leadership culture. Many families are looking for leadership that feels more approachable, modern, and student-focused rather than authority-driven.
#4 The appointment of Lundy as president has been a very positive change. He is approachable, engaged with students, visible within the school community, and makes an effort to know students personally, which creates a much stronger sense of connection and leadership.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
#1 Improve teacher accountability and communication with students. Too often, students send emails regarding important academic matters and do not receive responses in a timely manner, leaving them uncertain and unsupported. Setting clearer expectations around communication and response times would greatly improve the student experience.
#2 Consider implementing term limits for members of the Board of Directors (for example, a maximum of five years as is the case in most business professional environments) to encourage fresh perspectives and stronger governance. It may also be beneficial to review potential conflicts of interest when board members are parents or individuals who may indirectly benefit from decisions made by the school.
#3 Reevaluate the role and structure of student discipline leadership. The current approach can feel overly punitive and outdated rather than supportive and student-focused. A more modern model centered on mentorship, student wellbeing, accountability, and restorative practices may better reflect the values of a contemporary school community.

column15:
In my judgment, ALT (for grades 9 and 10) and ILT (for grades 11 and 12) need to be eliminated.  During ALT, students often seem tired (as they move toward the end of a 110 minute period), and classes often, although not always, seem to degenerate into hangout sessions.  During ILT, students typically use the time as a rest or hangout period; 30 minutes between classes simply isn't enough time to travel to a work location (if a quiet one can be found), begin working, and then pack up to go to another class.  In short, there isn't enough time to enter the "flow" state that is required for serious work.  The most rational decision, therefore, is to socialize or relax--and this seems to be, from my perspective, how most students use the ILT period.

I would suggest returning to a traditional schedule (e.g., the schedule used pre-2020).  We also shouldn't underestimate the benefit of finishing the school day earlier for senior students.  Before Covid, the senior school finished at 2:30 p.m., and this allowed extracurriculars and tutorials to start and finish at a more reasonable time. column14: Any additional comments about your experience or the College?
column15: Work/life balance is hard. There is a lot of outside of school hours commitments that make it hard to balance both work and life. Maybe putting a schedule C after parent teacher interviews that allows us to sleep in the next day, is a good alternative. As well, not being able to leave until 3:30pm is frustrating when 3-4 days a week we are stuck after school doing tutorial or sports or clubs, so on the days that I would like to leave after the bell, it is tough knowing I need to stay another 30 minutes, which is 30 minutes that could be going towards commute time home. Another suggestion would be putting schedule D's throughout the whole year, not just in the spring - coaches in the spring never get to experience the schedule D because they are always coaching. Winter teams play just as much as spring teams.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
- assessment and evaluation procedures need to be reviewed - Del needs expertise in this area 
- diversify the type of learning that is taking place in the classroom start to incorporate strategies to increase student participation in learning.  I see students as passive learners and it is a teacher centred learning environment.  Especially in junior school students should be "doing more stuff" rather than sitting at their desks.  An example can be science - junior school kids should be outside more, exploring and engaging with learning rather than just textbook interaction. There should be a difference in teaching and learning in junior vs senior school.
-length of school year should be reviewed - consider spacing out the academic year so that learning takes places well into June for grades 5-10.  Seems as though some of the stress affecting students might be due to the condensed school year.   
-detention procedures need to be reviewed.  Frequency and reasoning behind many detentions are not fair. Example is giving out detentions for forgetting classroom materials, this seems unjust. 
-some months are very heavy for teachers, many evening events and extra curriculars.  Parent teacher interviews 2 nights in Nov and Feb can be restructured. Consider balancing duties/evening events

column15:
Quality of teachers - a lot of the teachers appear to be very new and with little to no experience. This has caused classroom management issues, gaps in teaching/learning and issues with communication with parents. They also stay a year and then leave. I would prefer some more experienced and knowledgeable teachers and those that can interact and teach teens better. Hiring more qualified and better for teachers will also help with retention. 

Student learning support - on paper it seems like there are lots of resources to support learning when students are struggling but it hasn’t been very effective in our experience. As parents we are notified late that there are challenges happening and then long periods between assessments to check in on comprehension. Extra help and tutorials can be helpful but depending on the teacher they also may not (see above). Also the schedule now has extra help conflicting with others so you have to pick which to go to when you really need to attend both. I would love more support from guidance and a more collaborative program between teachers, guidance and student to check in in shorter periods to be more on top and correct sooner.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Communications: 1) Please provide updates to when Lunches will be provided earlier than the evening before. Many of us prepare kids lunches, all to find out they will be fed, or have a special day late into the evening. 2) Please ensure that all clubs/sports dates, times, and especially practices are well communicated with Parents as well. Emails are easier than schoology especially for the 10 and 11 year olds. 

Missing School for Valid Reasons: My children get significant anxiety knowing they have to miss school for a medical appointment or when they have a hockey tournament once or twice. Although they are not away that much (less than 5 times per year), the amount of anxiety to get homework from teachers is absolutely ridiculous. For your information, parent chats are usually exploding over weekends during winter months when kids are sick or are away with activities - all because teachers - not all - but MOST - absolutely refuse to respond to emails from parents/kids about what their homework will be. My children, and I would bet to offer many others, have significant anxiety about missing school because of this. I would say this needs to be fixed immediately. This is hugely problematic and needs to be investigated.

Class Time: I'm not sure I entirely understand why we have gone to an 8 day schedule - nowhere in the world is there a school as such. Given this, the impact has been to reduce time in class with all subjects. I have now compared with my son learned in 2023 for Grade 5 and what my younger son is learning now in Grade 5. The amount of work has nearly been cut in half. The amount of books read has been reduced. The amount of science learned reduced. This must be fixed next year. 

Exams Running both Semesters: I'd like to better understand why students need to be examined on materials in June that were taught in September and examined in December. I don't believe there are any schools that do this. Even universities are semestered and don't do this. I'm not sure the value here. I'd like to see this topic reviewed in detailed to ensure it makes sense and sets the kids up for success. 

Computers: These need to be replaced. My son continually receives computers that don't allow him to do his computers work at school. Please consider for funding next year.

Cafeteria Food: I wonder if the menu and food prices can be reviewed for next year. Seems as though the food choices are not the healthiest and are also very expensive. The boys are begging to have Calamari Friday's back - that was their favourite. 

Teachers that could benefit from coaching and mentorship: Ms. Pelliccione. Completely misaligned in their approach.

Bussing: The school should offer bussing service to communities. There is already one for woodbridge and should be one in Etobicoke. All other private schools offer this service.

I find that this year workload is much harder to balance because there is less time during the day to work on it and it takes longer when you cannot find or speak to a teacher who teaches that subject. I found that last year because the classes were shorter but smaller the learning was more effective. The length made the teachers teach lessons without over complicating them and was more straightforward. The size helped lead a more discussion based class which help understanding and application. This doesn’t happen as frequently now that everyone is in class at the same time and classes are bigger.

column15: The one thing that makes me so happy is the ban on cell phones during the school day. I hope teachers and staff will continue to enforce this ban - I have heard that perhaps more people are going to the washroom during the day to use their phones. It is crucial for phones to be away and out of sight for our children to be able to concentrate and focus on their teachers, classmates and the lessons. I also appreciate my child's teachers who reach out with good news or with items that are causing concern. The Parent Association is extremely dedicated in offering the Shoppe and the various special events for parents and for students.  I feel that DeLaSalle is an active and vibrant place with opportunities to develop every aspect of my child's growth.

column15:
Better professional development opportunities focused on the skills you wish every person possesses. More training on the platforms available and different resources meant to support students and faculty. More active mentorship and monitoring of staff and students. Continuous initiatives to recognize the effort of every member of the community and highlight the values we wish to promote, as well as the support. Better use of the science/math offices and writing centre by holding them when students have free time.

(For instance a prayer intention box in the chapel or a box with the name of all members of the student body and staff) so that anyone can offer 1 prayer for one person and then put it on the covered side to ensure we pray for everyone. "buddy benches" where students can sit to indicate they would like someone to reach out/invite them to participate. Beside sport facilities it would signify they would like to play with other students/join in on a game, in the upper campus that they would like to chat or sit and read, in the cafeteria to mean an open table and anyone to please come join (color-code benches to help with ambiguity). Sign-up boards for student-student tutoring somewhere where anyone can sign-up for help or offer help (to promote asking for help, service within the community and the recognition/promotion of talents of each individual) and a way to ensure the initiative is working as it should teachers of that subject/area would be in charge of linking them through email and students will be asked to always cc one of the teachers in any communication along with a feedback mechanism. Because this would require more administrative work from teachers it could also be a responsibility of student services or a different office or a new position (but that would still require teachers to "veto" the students offering help. A new office could also be helpful with managing community-building activities like culture day, etc.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Communications and Systems: 
- improved and streamlined communication to parents and students: all communications in one place and categorized rather than in series of lengthy emails, through a tool that is clear and easily searchable 
- acquiring an LMS or fully utilizing tools like Schoology (to better support busy parents and put more onus on students)

Academic Support and Assessment
- clear plan for students whose academic output is below school's high academic standards - shared observations among teachers, with referral to Student Services to create a targeted plan if student is struggling in more than one area
- curriculum leadership from department heads that includes aligning programs with current curriculum, sourcing up-to-date resources, offering PD to teachers, and creating a cohesive and progressive learning plan in each discipline
- ongoing PD and/or leadership role dedicated to improving assessment to align with current best practices in education. For ex: learning skills recognized as such and not addressed with punitive practices like detention (which is not consistently assigned among teachers or tracked to assess effectiveness); triangulation of assessment data (eg. conversation, observation, product)
- leadership role for junior school separate from senior school
- reporting on learning skills
- coherent plan and tracking system for discipline and academic expectations - uniform expectations across teachers with consistent consequences and a centralized tracking system that is shared with both Student Services and Office to support classroom management, discipline and academic standards (students are receiving many one-off detentions with no structured follow-up, no sharing of information and no means of monitoring whether this leads to improvements in academic achievement or student behaviour)
- clarity on purpose and benefits of ILT and ALT (if retained with new schedule) - unstructured time should be age-appropriate and aimed at improving student learning and establishing the appropriate tone for highly academic learning environment - time should be used for study and not regarded as "free time"
- fewer disruptions to learning, particularly for junior school

Strategic Alignment and Reputation
- integrated vision for admissions, advancement and academics that boosts school reputation in broader community, with an aim to improve perception of organization as a whole, acknowledge student achievement and boost income from donations

Work Environment
- consistent workspace provided for teachers - staffroom is currently very messy and only useable for small spurts of work (inefficient use of time and unprofessional look to prospective students, donors and staff); alternate spaces provided to teachers is temporary and does not support a focused and serious work environment

column15:
- Formative work: students should be given opportunities to practise what they are assessed on and to receive teacher feedback without being marked (on all homework).
- If students are not achieving good marks, tutorials should not be optional.
- Reach Ahead should be optional in the Junior school.
- Summer school for junior school students wanting to fill gaps (not for credit)
- Inconsistent teacher transparency. Some teachers are fantastic with student support, and some are very passive. Some teachers expect students, who miss school, to catch up with fellow classmates. This causes a lot of stress for students who may not be able to text friends to get homework. Teachers should post test outlines at minimum on schoology. column15:
- I wish there were more recreational sports in the juniors school.  Most of them are competitive or require experience so it feels exclusionary to students who may not have the same athletic background or ability. 
- better communication and transparency when it comes to disciplinary action.  For example, some schools have “incident reports” which are shared with staff, parent association and board members. The report does not identify anyone involved but it outlines the incident and the action that was taken.  This helps manage expectations on all levels and reinforces our ability to feel confident that the school takes appropriate action.  
- work harder to remove the subculture of “snitches get stitches” and encourage students to have the courage to come forward with the truth. Communicated to the students in a way that has a “real life” connection for our children and not only a biblical lesson.  Perhaps starting with something small like a “star ballot” where students have 1 or 2 weeks to put a ballot in a box with the name of another student that helped them or did something nice. At the end of the period each student who received a ballot will receive 1 point towards a pizza lunch for their class. The class with the most points wins.  I am sure there are parents that would help with this endeavour and also sponsor the pizza for this cause.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Academics - Need to move away from rewarding memorization to giving student opportunities to demonstrate integration and understanding of issues...  E.g. more class presentations/discussion.. possibly small group tutorials. Instead there seems to be more class work periods and supervised homework completion time is not the most effective use of classroom time. Knowledge of concepts and ability to synthesize information more important than knowledge of specific facts. Curriculum should also incorporate discussion/teaching on ethical and effective use of AI. Instead of shying away from AI there should be some opportunities to use AI with focus on how to use effectively and ethically. I am concerned that school's current academic approaches are less effective at engaging boys vs girls. 
Clubs - Consider offering some co-curriculars on different days of the week - right now my children can't participate in some activities due to scheduling conflicts. 
Facilities - Main Building - need to improve cleanliness (washrooms) and ventilation. If funding is an issue for this - please consider a specific fundraising initiative for this. We would be happy to contribute.  
Faith formation - After school activities to encourage continued faith formation (Alpha program? Theology of the Body? Bible Study etc.. ... Ensure students are well supported in their faith formation and can gain support/fellowship from peers/faculty)
Consideration of intramural Athletic opportunities to allow/encourage students to be physically active - even if not on varsity teams. Hope new Student Life Centre will be available for general use after school next year? Need to hear more about how the school will use the new student life centre.
