column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
Teaching/Teacher Standards and Quality:
The standards and quality of teachers have fallen from 4-5 years ago. Younger and new teachers don't hold the same depth in their lessons as the tenure teachers.  One of our students pointed out that, the only department that has a consistent roster of great/quality teachers is the English department. Our grade 12 student (and entire grade) has consistently complained to Student Services about the Physics teacher for not teaching the material, students don't know what/how to prepare for assessments.  This has been going on for a few years, why is there nothing done about it?  There needs to be an onboarding process of new teachers and perhaps the tenured teachers could offload best practices to new/YOUNG teachers.  
Del has a surplus budget, invest those funds in finding and RETAINING quality teachers.
 
Teacher Support:
Not all students learn the same way or thrive on one teaching method. Given the small class sizes at Del, teachers should be able to detect gaps in their students' learning and provide targeted support in the way that students need it most.  This is demonstrated however inconsistently, and at times, only privy to students that the teachers favour most.  We have heard from many other families of the same observation, and it is disheartening to students who know they are not being treated equally.  Perhaps the teacher's duty and responsibilities need to be reviewed annually as a refresher.

Student Life:
Activities around student life need a radical change. As a community, we know Del students work hard and yet there seems to be very few activities to allow students to let loose and celebrate each other without a catch (i.e., pay for dress down, pay $2 to get into the school, etc.)  Every year it's a "rinse and repeat" with the same fundraising activities.   Those hallmark events are important, but how about putting a little focus on our students.  Some examples: create a dedicated relaxation space for students, running outdoor classes when the weather permits, hands on learning opportunities (e.g., field trips to Shakespeare plays when studying a Shakespeare novel, have professional/career days and bring quality people to speak on different careers (finance, teaching, engineering, sports, etc.). Organize field trips that will help enrich students' university program choices by exposing students to different professional environments (Toronto Stock Exchange, Upper Canada Law Society, Sick Kids, etc.).

Sports Fees are too High:
$250 to play a school sport is expensive considering the tuition fee increased recently.  Consider refunding 50%.

Streamline your Tech!:
There are so many different portals for different things. Streamline your portals, provide a SSO to access every platform.  

School Trips that Make Economical Sense:
We have friends with kids attending public school, this year the school took their grade 10 students to England, Portugal and Spain for $5000.  Travel trips at Del are so expensive and there is little value for the price paid. Example: Italy trip 2025, 96 students, 1 tour guide, returning to hotels with a history of bedbugs, chicken and potatoes as the main food on the menu most nights for $10,000.  Introduce a transparent (provide the option for parents to vote) vetting process every two years allowing other travel companies to bring forth proposals. Volunteers/Chaperones pay 50% of their costs if they choose to attend. 

Quality & Pricing of Cafeteria:
The cafeteria menu could use a re-fresh and lower price points.  Bring back free food after 3:30/4:00pm Fridays!

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
1. The extracurricular schedule, and communication has come a little late overall, making it hard to schedule and balance with outside of school involvements. Also, certain clubs were listed on the original timetable which then were either not offered, or offered at a reduced schedule. 

2. I also feel strongly about the importance and potential of the music program. I completely understand that this is not an arts-specific school; however, hearing the Principal speak so passionately about the value of a strong arts education made it clear that the arts are considered an important part of the school’s identity, something I very much appreciate and support.

While the fine arts program overall is wonderful, I believe the music department has the capacity to grow even further. There is a great deal of talent among the students, and music education offers benefits that extend well beyond artistic development, including confidence, discipline, collaboration, and emotional well-being.

I believe students would benefit tremendously from a mandatory choir program led by an experienced and highly trained music educator. I also feel there could be higher expectations and more structured instruction on instrumental training, which would help students build stronger musical skills and confidence over time.

3. In last year’s brochure, it was noted that promoting healthy eating choices in the cafeteria is an important priority, and I appreciate the effort being made to move away from typical “junk food” options. While there are certainly some healthy choices available, it still seems that the majority of main meal offerings - both in the cafeteria and the Del Shoppe - lean toward less healthy options.

It may be worthwhile to further encourage healthier eating habits by limiting some of the less nutritious choices altogether and placing greater emphasis on balanced, wholesome options for students.

column15: As a student who has now experienced Flex Mode schedule as well as the new one i can confidently say i prefer the 2024/2025 school year schedule by a lot. With alt many teacher teach through it meaning you are in a classroom sitting for an hour and a half straight of someone teaching, personally the exceed my limits and many other student not only the teaching and new material but the overall class time and lack of breaks. A 40 minute lunch is not nearly enough time to decompress in a 7 hours heavy duty school day. Aswell as I was quite excited to come to del for the unique and well structured schedule. It seemed and was perfect and the most ideal schedule. I enjoyed more than 4 classes a day including breaks and overall the way it was executed.Personally i used my ILT time to study and socialize. Socializing is a crucial part of the high school experience not only to just talk but make new friends and get comfortable to a new community. With this new schedule we are also restricted to only seeing grade 9 and 10 like many we have friends in either grades above or below and now many can’t see them at any time of the day due to the lack of breaks and minimal outside of class time. Socializing with other students other than our grade can help grow our social and communication skills. To continue, me and many of other students found office hours extremely affect and helpful. Now i have to sacrifice my only break of the my day, my lunch to attend some tutorials and now have an overwhelming day due to lack of breaks and time to decompress, overall it’s a very full and compact day and I feel it’s not right for 14-17 year old to experience this. The overall 2 day schedule is not beneficial whatsoever and i find i’m more stressed now because if i miss one day then i have back to back classes and i will not be prepared for those classes leading me to stress and failure. I am not only saying this because we want more free time i genuinely feel it’s way to much time in a classroom for a day and many can’t focus for that long of a period.Another issue I have personally experienced as a grade 9 and current and almost finished grade 10 student I feel as though the lack of quality in teacher for the new highschool grades. I’ve experienced and currently is dealing with almost under qualified teachers who don’t really know what they are doing and feels like a public school teaching style. Many don’t know how to teach and many other students agree and this results in very poor grade outcomes. Many if not all of the grade 11 and 12 teachers seem very qualified and very much know what they are doing not saying they don’t have flaws but they have flaws that are easy to fix and understand. Many of my teachers past or present have seemed to not know what they are taking about, don’t teacher properly or at all!!! And when teachers and faculty come to sit in it’s all and act and most of the time that will be the only productive class of the year.  I would appreciate looking more into teachers before hiring and not keep hiring new teachers for the lower senior school because it really affects how you learn and will set you up for failure in future year to come, especially at del. I pay for this and I’m not spending 20,000 on teachers who can’t teach well or think it’s a hassle to teach when that is their job.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
1. 8 Day Schedule (ineffective)
The current 8-day schedule system can be ineffective because students do not spend enough consistent time learning certain subjects. The long gaps between classes can make it difficult for students to retain information and stay fully engaged with the material being taught. I also believe that having an 8-day rotation can be overwhelming and confusing for students to keep track of. Compared to a shorter and more consistent schedule, the current system may create unnecessary stress and make it harder for students to maintain organized routines and balanced workloads.
2. Communication with Teachers (poor communication)
The communication process regarding missed work is a challenge. Students are often instructed to email teachers when they are absent in order to catch up on assignments or class material. However, in many cases, teachers do not respond to these emails or take a very long time to reply. This can leave students confused about what they missed and make it difficult to stay caught up academically after an absence. I would also like to mention that communication issues do not only affect students, but parents as well. There have been situations where I, or other parents I know, have emailed teachers with questions or concerns and have not received responses in a reasonable amount of time, or sometimes no response at all.
3. Sports and Clubs
I appreciate the effort that the coaches and staff put into organizing clubs and sports activities for students. However, scheduling for practices, games, and club meetings often seems to be inconsistent or communicated at the last minute. In many cases, schedules are not posted in advance, which can make it difficult for students and parents to plan transportation and arrange pickup times after school. Last-minute changes or announcements can create unnecessary stress for us families trying to coordinate their schedules.
4. Teaching Staff (poor communication)
I have concerns regarding the quality and consistency of teaching this year. While there are many dedicated and hardworking teachers at the school, there have also been several situations where students have struggled due to teachers lacking the necessary teaching, communication, or classroom management skills needed to effectively support student learning. These issues have had an impact on students’ academic experiences and overall confidence in certain classes. I believe it is important that the school continues to prioritize hiring qualified, experienced, and supportive educators who are well-prepared to meet students’ educational needs.
5. Safety 
I would also like to raise a serious concern regarding students entering and exiting the school grounds through Farnham Road. The area becomes very busy during arrival and dismissal times, and I am worried about student safety because of the traffic and congestion. There have been situations where cars have driven onto the sidewalk area, which is extremely dangerous and could easily result in a student being injured. With so many students walking in that area, the current traffic situation feels unsafe.  Can an alternative entry or exit point be considered?
6. Schoology (inconsistent use)
Another concern is that Schoology is not being consistently used by all teachers. I believe it would be very beneficial if all teachers regularly used the platform to post assignments, updates, class materials, and important messages. When some teachers do not update Schoology consistently, it can become difficult for students to stay informed about schoolwork, deadlines, and classroom expectations, especially if they are absent. Having all teachers use the same platform in a consistent way would improve communication, organization, and help students stay up to date with their learning.
7. Communication with Students while on trips
Teachers do not consistently communicate updates to parents about return times.
8. Clear Schedules with start and end times

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
The academic program is quite disappointing and does not adequately challenge my children. 

Based on the entrance exams and the admission process I expected an academically rigorous program that will push my children. Academic rigour is not about the number of hours of homework and/or excessive work load but rather teaching our children to be deep critical thinkers and challenge their thinking in a safe / nurturing / catholic context.

Lower School :  We experienced that the academic program for gr 5 and 6 was primarily a repeat of what my child did in gr 3/4 (particularly math, French, English and Science) at their previous independent school. My child is not being challenged at DLS as the academic program is teaching to the lowest common denominator rather than providing a differentiated learning experience. Students with high academic potential need to be challenged or they get bored / disengaged and assume learning will always continue to come easy.

High School: For my other child, who joined the school in grade 9 this year coming from an independent school with advanced academics the gr 9 academic program at DLS did not provide an academic challenge. Our experience is that the gr 9 program (except for English) was focused on repeating concepts taught in grs 7 / 8.  The DLS gr 9 program is overly focused on passively repeating information through memorization as noted in many of the quizzes and tests in the various gr 9 courses.  I suggest that the gr 9 academic program needs to focus more on critical thinking and intellectual growth rater than memorization. The acquisition and recall of information through repetition does not serve anyone well in 2026 where AI can provide most of this information and as such recall is not a key skill. The ability to think critically and analyze are key skills that needed in 2026.

column15: De La Salle could benefit from reviewing the overall homework load assigned to students. At times, students are managing 3–4+ hours of homework per night, which makes it difficult to balance academics with extracurriculars and personal well-being. Given that the curriculum is already well ahead of many other schools, a modest reduction in take-home work would go a long way. Additionally, the current 8-day rotating schedule creates some imbalance — certain classes only occur once per week, leading to long gaps and unnecessary confusion for students. A simpler Day 1/Day 2 alternating schedule would provide more consistency and better pacing across all subjects.

column15:
Communication:
Communication needs to be streamlined. 
A proper Communication or LMS need to be adopted and properly used. 
It should not be up to the parents to find out what homework was missed or the ones to take photos of handouts and send to other parents  (this is happening whether the school wants this to happen or not). All class info should be posted online for students. Parents could easily see when teachers assigned homework and marks of assessments can be posted and reviewed by parents on said platform. Consider the Edsby platform. 
The volume and length of emails is unacceptable. In the month of May I've received nearly 30 emails from the school. No one needs this, parents are incredibly busy and the amount of information in one email is overwhelming. The grade reps are constantly having to remind parents about special events, schedule changes or  anything that is shared in an email simply because people cannot keep up with the info. There is always a handful of people that did not receive the email. 

General Academics:
More updates or context for student learning.  What are the students learning and why? Assuming the school is working using the Ontario curriculum as a framework, what is happening that enriches or enhances the learning? How is my child developing in relation to learning skills? 
More experiential learning opportunities. Class trips that provide rich  and meaningful learning experiences.

Junior School and Exams:
Junior school student do not need exams - specifically grade 5/6s there is no evidence suggesting this prepares them academically.  Junior school students need to be in school up until all high school students finished exams. The last two weeks should be an opportunity for students to create learning portfolios or culminating projects or self directed inquiry projects. 

A.I.
How is Del preparing students to live and work in a world that will be dominated by A.I? Guidelines and policies that go beyond - pen and paper tasks need to be adopted to prepare students. Course work should be reflective of the changing landscape in education.

column15:
Certain subjects are not in line with the Ontario curriculum. For example Canadian history versus modern Christian martyr investigation, founders of Christendom -all interesting topics but there is a curriculum and should be followed. Science curriculum has been lacking and needs to be revisited. These are important foundational subjects that should be taught to the kids inline with the curriculum and on a regular basis. 

The schedule  needs to be revisited as this year it was concerning how many times some kids actually had a subject and remember what was taught between classes. Top of mind is Science, between the schedule whereby science would be so far apart and then even further if there was an event/holiday or the teacher was off with extra curricular. 

Cafeteria - in discussion with various kids/parents the food is awful and just keeps getting worse each year while the prices keep increasing. While price increase is somewhat out of our hands due to the world we are in today, the quality of food is within our control. The cafeteria has been a point of discussion for many years and nothing is being done to find a solution which also raises concerns. While change is hard if it is not working then something should be done to fix/remedy this. 

Pay as you go activities - this deters certain kids from participating. Having the lump sum fee helps to provide a nudge (by the parents) to those kids who are on the fence or would rather not participate. School is a perfect opportunity to try different things!

Changes to the curriculum/schedules should be discussed with the parents especially if it takes away from core curriculum!!

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
The communication recently sent to parents regarding “most updated grades” and “current grades” was completely inaccurate. In several courses, marks have not been updated since early in 2026 (winter months), yet families are being told these are students’ "current"standings before exams.
If teachers are unable or unwilling to keep gradebooks updated, then the school should not present these marks as accurate representations of student performance. Students are expected to stay on top of deadlines all semester, so it is reasonable for parents to expect the same level of accountability when it comes to grading updates. Student stress levels are already extremely high prior to final exams and so it is unacceptable that families are expected to make sense of outdated and incomplete information before exams. Either ensure teachers are keeping PowerSchool current, or stop advertising these visibility windows as showing “updated” grades when they clearly do not.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Two issues related to the availability and timing of extracurriculars could be improved.  First, many/most of the sports teams are very competitive and offer minimal opportunities for students who are not involved in these sports at a high level.   A "B Team" should be considered to allow everyone who wants to participate in these teams an opportunity to do so.  Second, morning practices are too early.  Teenagers require 8 to 10 hours of sleep per night for optimal brain development, mood regulation, and academic success and it's not possible to get enough sleep with a morning practice starting at 6:50 or 7:00 am.

Also, the school needs to consider and develop a plan to deal with AI (eg., ChatGPT) usage by students.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15: The issue of AI needs some serious attention.  See the recent studty from MIT’s Media Lab and its concerning results.  The study divided 54 subjects into three groups, and asked them to write several SAT essays using OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s search engine, and nothing at all, respectively. Researchers used an EEG to record the writers’ brain activity across 32 regions, and found that of the three groups, ChatGPT users had the lowest brain engagement and “consistently underperformed at neural, linguistic, and behavioral levels.” Over the course of several months, ChatGPT users got lazier with each subsequent essay, often resorting to copy-and-paste by the end of the study.  This issue needs serious attention as the brain development that occurs during the high school years can never be recovered in the future.

column15: I made this comment in last year’s survey and it appears that the college is still moving forward with this so I thought I would mention it again. I don’t have a lot of details, but my understanding is that there’s some kind of harassment reporting line being set up for students to be able to report bullying or claims of insults, including racism and what has been described as “hate“. Subject to finding out more about this, I caution about promoting this kind of initiative given the misunderstandings that can happen among teenagers and in the potential to create problems where some may not exist. Including by the way, getting into debates and arguments, potentially involving parents about interpretations, motives, etc. The school does a good job in my mind of teaching tolerance through the Bible and it should continue to do that without suggesting that there is hate and racism at the school, which in my mind I have seen zero evidence of in my two years at the school.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
- If surveys are intended to be anonymous, the questions should feel less personally identifying. Some prompts are so specific that respondents may hesitate to answer honestly out of concern they could be identified.- Focus less on rigid image and optics, and more on creating a balanced, supportive student experience. Academic rigour is important, but so is student morale, mental health, and fostering a positive school culture. - The role and approach of the “Director of Discipline” feels overly old-fashioned and authoritarian. The system could benefit from a more modern, student-centered approach focused on mentorship and respect rather than punishment and control. - Some staff members make students and parents uncomfortable. The school should take concerns about professionalism, student comfort, and appropriate conduct seriously and ensure all staff interactions foster trust and safety. - School events, initiatives, and traditions feel repetitive year after year, especially for long-term students. While traditions are important, introducing new ideas, activities, and experiences would help keep students engaged and make the community feel more dynamic. - More student voice should be incorporated into decision-making. Students are the ones experiencing the school environment daily, and there should be more meaningful opportunities for them to provide input on policies, events, and school culture.
- Improve communication and responsiveness when concerns are raised. Families should feel heard rather than dismissed, especially when discussing academics, wellbeing, or fairness.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
-Schedule: a few minutes between classes is needed for washroom breaks
-Communal lunch: I often eat lunch quietly/on my own because colleagues are working and don't share the same lunch time which takes away from trying to build a sense of belonging
-Discipline structure: I've been most impacted this year with a lack of discipline structure, I have been sent around from one admin/counsellor to another to get some support about discipline issues and the delay in dealing with something that came up and effecting classroom dynamics, was very discouraging and frustrating. Classes kept going but issues didn't seem important enough to deal with hence being sent from one person to the next with no one taking action or promising to do something about a situation, and then delay by an unacceptable amount of time.
-Equality: there is apparent favouritism which will naturally be denied because it sounds bad but it's evident that some staff members get what they want fast, are helped right away, and are recognised immediately, and some not.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
Final exams - there should be a blackout period of two weeks before final exams (my kids are being tested on May 27; one child has two tests). 

Feedback - I think parents need to be given feedback / visibility into grades between January to May - to not have feedback or an idea of grading for 4-5 months is too long of a gap

Grade 7 math teacher - on her phone in class a lot (this is not appropriate); uses AI to reply to emails from parents (as a parent I dislike this and feel the email reply is not tailored to my questions/ concerns/ child); doesn’t hand assessments back for 3-5 weeks (that’s too long); doesn’t reply to parent emails; very concerned with students doing the math her way or they don’t get full marks despite a correct answer and a different approach; prepared tests that are too long for the class time in the schedule

Music - there needs to be organized opportunities for musicians in the school and communications about these opportunities in a timely manner; a senior school music trip would be a wonderful opportunity for senior school music students; more excitement and motivation needed in the music program; will a head of music be recruited? This seems to be part of the problem - not having a head of the department 

Science - concern that an Ontario curriculum item didn’t happen in grade 10 (dissection of the frog) 

Field trips - there was 1 field trip in grade 7 and it was to a movie; can there be some exciting and relevant field trips planned for the grade 8s next year? Would be nice for some experiential learning experiences which are relevant to curriculum items

Experiential trips - these are lacking; it would be great for senior students to be able to volunteer in third world countries etc; or to explore a new place (outside of the Italy offering)

House system - would be nice to have a house cup so that the students are encouraged to live out their Lasallian values for house points (and other criteria). Students will be engaged, excited and motivated. Updates can be given at assembly.

Curriculum / lesson planning - who at the school oversees the curriculum and lesson plans at the school to make sure the academic rigour is high at del? Concerned that this is not happening (esp after what happened in grade 7 science this year)

column15: I understand that extra curricular activities are a selling point for the College and we must compete against other schools in this regard, but there is far too many things going on that take the students  outside of class. I also understand the counterargument to my point, but in the end, when the marks are submitted to the university, these activities are not part of the grade, the are not considered in the course, and the main educational/academic purpose of this institution is waning. Clearly, the College offers wonderful extra curricular opportunities, but many students are stretched too thin. As a result, mental and physical anxiety, lower evaluations are the result, mostly due to  missed class work. I suggest that one of the teaching staff's main frustration is that too many students are absent too often (I hear this loud and clear in the staff room areas. So, students receive some outside class adventure, but their evaluations suffer, so this is really a zero-sum gain. I believe students should be in class as their primary duty (just like workers are wanted back in the office) and all these extra activities should work in concert and in support of this obligation. It seems, however, that the opposite is the case, and these adventures & activities are dominating the academic schedule and effective instructional time. This is a mistake and a greater balance is needed.

column15:
Junior school- to support transition more teacher feedback is needed to support student/behavior/progress. If there is a behaviour/progress concerns they should be shared right away before they become habit forming. If there are infractions/behaviors an email should be shared so home and school can work together. 
Independent Reading program- students should engage in a more structured reading program that offers reading books based on reading level and a comprehension quiz is provided. (i.e. Accelerated Reader by Renaissance learning) The school can incentivize number of books read with student rewards. 
Highschool- careers/civics class should spend more time exploring university programs/options to help coach them to find a path. Allocate scheduled time with a councillor to check in and prioritize future programs. 
Parent Calendar- should also share dates of sports meets, club events and key dates to reduce overlap regarding school school sports/club events. 
Student recognition- pins/awards to recognize student achievement and incentivize student performance. 
Increase the number of travel/field trip/ guest speaker opportunities to enhance real world connections.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
1) Independent Learning Time (ILT):  Our child previously had time to go to their teachers' office hours but with the current schedule, they are not able to do so as they are required to stay in for ILT in classrooms replacing the time they would otherwise have free to attend office hours of their choice.  They have also commented that not all teachers use this supervised ILT in the same way - some use it to continue teaching new content; some for time to do homework from the class the teacher leads and others let students do homework from other classes.  It would be good to have more opportunity for students to have time to attend ILT with content experts in areas of most value to students.

2) Quality of Teaching:  Our child has also said that not all teachers have comparable teaching abilities.  Some are excellent but others seem to direct the students to self teach from the textbook/online content and provide little teaching themselves.  I suggest having more in class review of teaching styles and effectiveness from the school principal/vice-principal to ensure high teaching quality in all classes.

3) Faith in Action:  I suggest having more opportunities for students to discuss how they practically apply their Catholic faith in their everyday lives akin to Alpha Group dinners with honest sharing of experiences and practical examples of solutions where students feel torn in different directions.

4) Quiet Study Space:  I suggest having more quiet spaces for studying such as a library/study centre both during school hours and before and after hours - the cafeteria is very noisy and makes it challenging to do work

5) Nutritious food:  I suggest increasing the nutritional value of the food in the cafeteria with whole grain breads/muffins and healthier snacks.

column14: Please share any suggestions that would help De La Salle College improve.
column15:
1) Del should recalibrate its grading in grades 11 and 12 so that students can be admitted into the top universities/programs of their choice. While calibration appears to be occurring late in grade 12 that is often too late as universities have offered a large proportion of spots based on grade 11 or early grade 12 results. While Del prides itself on its high academic standards and preparing students for university, that should be balanced with ensuring that students are treated fairly in getting into university/program of choice. 

2) Del should consider whether its standards for permitting students to remain as students is appropriate. Students who are extremely and frequently disruptive, who engage in bullying and physical violence and who do not understand that their actions are wrong should be severely punished, such students should be frequently reminded that their behaviour must improve and the school should consider if it is fair to other students that these disruptive students be permitted to remain at the school. Centralizing discipline would ensure fair treatment and identification of problem students. Staff who are conflicted should be recused from decisions relating to discipline of students. 

3) Administration is not consistent (and often not timely) in following up on parent concerns/questions. Certain staff members are more receptive and carry through with agreed actions whereas others are not.

column15:
Two areas where I believe the school can improve:

1. Communication and IT experience
    There are currently too many portals, apps, and communication channels. Important information is difficult to find and the overall experience feels fragmented. A simpler and more centralized communication strategy would significantly improve the parent and student experience. As someone who works in AI and technology strategy, I would be happy to provide feedback or help think through practical improvements if useful.
2. Facilities maintenance and student accountability
    The condition of some facilities, especially the bathrooms, needs improvement. Part of this is maintenance, but part is also student responsibility. Basic habits such as flushing toilets and respecting shared spaces go a long way. Setting clearer expectations around cleanliness and accountability would make a meaningful difference for everyone

column15:
I feel that the flex mod schedule helps children to learn how to better organize their time (my daughter has had 1 year with and 1 year without).
I understand the concerns with ALT vs ILT and I do agree for 9 and 10 and ALT model is best.  In my opinion this can be achieved by having an ALT class room when grade 9 and 10 go to for ALT and work on assignments in a quiet, organized and supervised setting.  for the older years I would hope that children use ILT go to areas where than can talk about group assignments and share ideas.

Different class sizes also given students a chance to experience a university environment.  In the previous model the change between grade 8 and  grade 9 was drastic but if there is a way to introduce class sizes slowly starting in grade 10 that would be great, or flex mod schedule in grade 9 and 10 then class size variation in 11 and 12 so that every year we are build the foundation to prepare our children for life outside of a structured class room.

column15: I thought my daughter’s teachers were great this year, but ALT was not properly implemented in all classes. While some teachers respected that ALT was time for students to quietly work on their homework, others either kept teaching throughout the entire ALT period or demanded that students work on the subject matter related to the ALT. As per my daughter, after 70 minutes of instruction in a certain course, it is very unappealing to then do homework for that subject matter and I do not disagree with that. While I understand that Mr. Lundy has been speaking to staff to make sure that they implement ALT properly, sadly, this is not the case for all teachers. As well, my daughter pointed out that they are not allowed to use their laptops during certain ALT periods, because some teachers do not allow it. This means that they cannot take advantage of the time that they have to advance in their work if that work is online, which in many cases it is. As Mr. Lundy pointed out, in order to remedy this, he stands either at the back of his class or walks in between rows, however, all teachers do not do this, and so they disallow the use of a laptop. In short, I would really love ALT to be what it is supposed to be, exactly as Mr. Lundy describes it and how he himself implements it in his math class.

column15:
ALT: As mentioned above, respecting ALT is something that I think is most important because it will prepare our students for university. 

IT: The different technology platforms that the school uses can be very confusing, especially for new parents, and this could benefit from an overhaul so as to make things more streamlined.

Gradebook Visibility: While I understand that year-round visibility might put more pressure on teachers, I think that it is done way too infrequently. For students who are doing well this is not a problem, however, I can imagine that for those who are having some trouble, gradebook visibility is very important, especially so that proper action can be taken to help the student students along.

Averages: I have been asking for averages to be included in the report card for years now after it was removed because I do not think that a grade is meaningful without the corresponding class average. Incidentally, this would reduce student anxiety around grades and would help put things in context.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
In my experience, De La Salle fosters an attitude among the students that rejects any form of individuality or difference which leads to unsavoury, antisocial behaviour. I have seen students mock others, use slurs, and behave disrespectfully to anyone who falls outside of “the norm.” I understand that this school is built on religious values, and there are some stances it must uphold, but it should not give students the excuse to treat one another so disgustingly. I have heard a plethora of disparaging comments launched against another student for something as simple as wearing a unique outfit on a dress-down day. Many students are much harsher when it comes to things such as identity. It becomes challenging to report these incidents because it has become such a ubiquitous and integrated element of our student community. Our students are often seen as respectful, and that may be true in some instances, but it is also true that there is a general air of intolerance and hate among us. 
       As a school that prides itself on community, I think it is imperative to address these concerns. “Community” should not be a superficial label used to advertise the school to newcomers. It should be a lived reality, but I have found more often than not that we are very far from it. The school should really emphasize respect and kindness. Simply telling students to behave that way is platitudinous. A paradigm shift is necessary for students to actually adopt these teachings in their heart. Otherwise, the performative kindness will continue, and the hateful undertones will remain. It certainly does not help that our private school tends to be very insular, preventing students from developing empathy for people of all backgrounds. Outreach programs may help resolve this. Moreover, students need to be punished adequately for acting antithetically to De La Salle’s values. They must understand the full consequences of such actions, not only as they damage their relationships with their peers, but also how they diminish the trust and care within the school community as a whole.
       Lastly, there should be more done to encourage individual expression. Again, I understand that there are some religious values that the school must uphold, but currently, students get mocked for dressing differently, performing during Del’s Got Talent, or showing any passion for anything beyond social media. Not only has this resulted in a tense and monotonous school environment, but it also reinforces itself. Students are now scared to pursue these things because they understand the negative social repercussions of doing so. If there was a more positive environment fostered, maybe students would be more emboldened to try new things, and maybe it would be seen as bizarre to ever consider embarrassing someone who does them. Individuality needs to be normalized if you want to form respectful, cultured individuals.

column15:
This school has a tumultuous relationship with mental health. I think it is great that we have been talking about these issues in recent years. Destigmatization is always the first step in broaching such a difficult subject. However, talking can only get us so far. Even when we acknowledge mental health, it does not fix the problem. Students are overworked, sleep-deprived, and under immense pressure, serving as a prime breeding ground for anxiety and depression. I know this school prides itself on being academically rigorous, but sometimes, it gets to an unreasonable degree. There is no reason why a singular teacher should place a large project and a test within a few days of one another for the same subject, but it has happened to me many times. It creates situations where even when a student spends countless hours studying, they must now dedicate even more time to doing additional coursework for the exact same subject, as well as for every other subject with immense amounts of work. For any student who wishes to do well, the solution is not to spend less time on each task- it is to sleep, socialize, and participate in extracurriculars less. There are simply not enough hours in the day to adequately commit to everything. The unnecessarily dense schedules that this school permits does not form well-rounded students, but instead students who are burnt out. If you want to address the mental health crisis at our school, looking at and amending what you are expecting of students would be a start.
       Moreover, students have nowhere to go. Student Services is advertised as the ideal party to approach with our woes, but they are not equipped with the skills, tools, or confidentiality to adequately address the very serious issues students face. Personally, I have avoided going to student services with my struggles because I have heard of their interactions with my friends, and each instance has shown them as dismissive or worsening the problem. I do not think their actions are malicious. I simply think they are inadequately trained to address mental health issues. I think introducing a school psychologist and therapist will help resolve this problem. These would be professionals who know how to deal with mental health issues in youth. These would be people students can go to and know that their information will be kept private. This is especially important for students struggling with familial issues or things they would not want their parents to know. This would create a safe space for students to have their mental health needs addressed, not just acknowledged.

Teacher involvement with students should be more. We found this year especially that our kids wanted to stay for tutorial however their teachers were not available to be there due to extra curricular activities or personal affairs. We feel that if a teacher cant make their tutorial there should be a make up day. 
Also the kids do seem overwhelmed with work load. Staying up far too late to complete work. The reality is that most kids now days are in sports or programs after school which keeps them off screens and engaged in community. Del needs to recognize this reality. We do want a challenging curriculum but their needs to be balance. 
We also believe the school should raise tuition. Even a slight raise would benefit the school, students, teachers and community. It would allow for more for the school to renovate, purchase new learning equipment and improve the campus. 
The cafeteria needs to be re done. We also need to offer our students healthier options. The Del shop should not be selling candy. We are in a new world. We are more knowledgeable about healthy eating and the effects of candy is not good and yet we are selling it to our students. Instead of having some many small events to raise fundstwhy not instead increase tuition to benefit the school in a way in which the school can plan forward.

column14: What should De La Salle improve most?
column15:
1. De-coupling marks from academic rigour.  Del teachers are taught to demonstrate academic rigour through tough marking that places students at a disadvantage to their public school peers when applying to universities.  I support strong academic rigour.  But you don't need to illustrate it by uniformly marking low.  I hear stories of teachers taking delight in marking an entire class in the 50s for a test.  That is not a failure of those students, it is a failure of the teacher.  Teachers can affirm their personal identities as being academically rigorous without illustrating it through tough marking.  The administration needs to hold teachers to account when they do this.  This is why it concerns me most...

2. Confidence.  Del's view is confidence is built by students learning to master a topic through discipline and hard work.  They mark tough in order to induce this process.  This works for some children but it prompts other children to retreat, like my child.  There are multiple paths to the same destination.  Your approach doesn't work for every child.  For many kids, confidence is built through an inverse process: building a healthy, self-confident identity which then leads to stronger performance.  Del needs to adapt its approach by prioritizing building confidence as a tool to creating strong performance by adopting an organizational growth mindset.  Study different approaches to building confidence.  Adopt a broader set of strategies.  You have taught my child a tremendous amount, built discipline, have been academically rigorous, but at the expense of his confidence.  He is a far less confident child academically than when he began at Del in grade 5. Del can do better but only if it adopts that growth mindset, decouples marking from academic rigour, and holds its teachers to account, not it students, when entire cohorts do poorly on specific assignments.
